regulation_content.regulation_text:
1. Short title and commencement
(1) These regulations may be called the International Financial Services Centres
Authority (Pension Fund) Regulations, 2026.

(2) These regulations shall come into force on and from the date of their publication in
the Official Gazette.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives the Regulations their short title and provides that they come into force on publication in the Official Gazette.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Notified 30 March 2026; in force on Gazette publication

regulation_content.regulation_text:
2. Objectives

These regulations provide the regulatory framework for registration, regulation and
supervision of the Pension Funds in the International Financial Services Centre in India,
with the objectives of establishing a robust framework for long-term retirement savings,
promoting a secure and transparent environment for subscribers, protecting their interests
and maintaining the integrity of the pension ecosystem in IFSC.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: States the object of the Regulations — to provide the framework for registration, regulation and supervision of Pension Funds in the IFSC, aimed at long-term retirement savings, subscriber protection and the integrity of the IFSC pension ecosystem.
regulation_content.applicability: All Pension Funds in the IFSC

regulation_content.regulation_text:
3. Definitions

(1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, the terms defined herein
shall bear the meanings as assigned to them below, and their cognate expressions shall
be construed accordingly, -

(a) “Act” means the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 (50
 of 2019);
(b) “Authority” means the International Financial Services Centres Authority
 established under the sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Act;
(c) “Board” refers to the Board of Directors of a Pension Fund;

(d) “Contribution” means the amount deposited by or on behalf of a Subscriber into
 his/her Pension Account;
(a) “Credit Rating Agency” means a person who is engaged in the business of rating
 of Securities, Financial Products, issuers or sovereigns, and is regulated by the
 Authority or other relevant financial sector regulator, in India or any foreign
 jurisdiction, as a credit rating agency;
(b) “Custodian” means a person who is engaged in the business of providing the
 services of safekeeping the Financial Products, and is regulated by the Authority
 or other relevant financial sector regulator, in India or any foreign jurisdiction, as
 a custodian;
(c) “Key Managerial Personnel” refers to the Chief Executive Officer, Chief
 Investment Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Compliance Officer, and such other
 officer who may be appointed/designated as Key Managerial Personnel by the
 Pension Fund;
(d) “Net Worth” means the aggregate value of the paid-up share capital and all
 reserves created out of the profits, securities premium account and debit or credit
 balance of profit and loss account, after deducting the aggregate value of the
 accumulated losses, deferred expenditure and miscellaneous expenditure not
 written off, as per the audited balance sheet, but does not include reserves created
 out of revaluation of assets, write-back of depreciation and amalgamation;
(e) “Pension Account” means an account opened by a Subscriber with a Pension
 Fund, which, inter-alia reflects the Subscriber’s contributions, investment returns
 and withdrawals;
(f) “Pension Fund” means an entity which has been granted a certificate of
 registration under these regulations by the Authority as a pension fund for
 receiving contributions, accumulating them and making payments to the
 Subscriber;
(g) “Scheme” means a scheme of Pension Fund approved by the Authority;
 Explanation.- Scheme shall be voluntary in nature and consisting of a specific
 investment option or product offered by a Pension Fund having distinct
 investment objectives, strategies, and risk profiles.
(h) “Scheme Information Document” means the document containing all material
 information including investment objectives, asset allocation strategy and risk
 profile about a specific Scheme offered by a Pension Fund;
(i) “Single Window IT System (SWIT)” refers to an online platform designed by the
 Authority, inter-alia to facilitate processing of the application submitted for
 obtaining certificate of registration under these regulations;
(j) “Subscriber” means any individual who is above the age of 18 years, and has
 voluntarily joined the Scheme and holds a Pension Account;
(k) “subsidiary instruction” shall have the same meaning as assigned to it under
 clause (e) of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 2 of the International Financial
 Services Centres Authority (Procedure for making regulations and subsidiary
 instructions) Regulations, 2025.
(l) “Systematic Withdrawal Plan” means a facility that allows a Subscriber to
 withdraw a predetermined amount at regular intervals from his accumulated
 corpus managed by a Pension Fund;

[भाग III—खण्‍ड 4] भारत‍का‍राजपत्र‍:‍असाधारण 35

(m) “Trustee” means a person appointed by the Pension Fund to hold the assets of the
 Scheme for the benefit of the Subscribers;
(n) “Unit” means a unit of the Scheme representing the fractional interest
 proportionate to Subscriber’s share in the corpus of the Scheme.
(2) Words and expressions used and not defined in these regulations but defined in the
Act or Acts mentioned in the First Schedule to the Act, or the Companies Act, 2013, or
any rules or regulations made thereunder shall have the same meanings respectively
assigned to them in those Acts, rules or regulations or any statutory modification or re-
enactment thereto, as the case may be.

 CHAPTER II
 REGISTRATION AND ELIGIBILITY OF PENSION FUND
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Defines the terms used across the Regulations, including Pension Fund, Pension Account, Subscriber (an individual above 18 who has voluntarily joined), Scheme (voluntary, with distinct investment objective/strategy/risk), Scheme Information Document, Trustee, Custodian, Systematic Withdrawal Plan, Net Worth, Unit and SWIT (the single-window IT system for applications).
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Two definitions do heavy structural work. A Scheme is voluntary and must be constituted as a trust (Regulation 13), so the Pension Fund and the Scheme are deliberately separated — the fund manages, the trust holds. And Net Worth is defined tightly to the audited balance sheet, excluding revaluation reserves, write-back of depreciation and amalgamation reserves, which matters for the continuing USD 1 million test in Regulation 5.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Subscriber = individual above 18; Scheme = voluntary, constituted as a trust; Net Worth excludes revaluation/write-back/amalgamation reserves

regulation_content.chapter_title: Registration And Eligibility Of Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
4. Registration

(1) No person shall act as a Pension Fund under these regulations unless it has obtained
a certificate of registration from the Authority as a Pension Fund.

(2) An entity desirous of obtaining a certificate of registration from the Authority as a
Pension Fund shall submit an application form through SWIT, accompanied by such fees
and documents and in such manner as may be specified by the Authority.

(3) The applicant, while making application, shall provide comprehensive details
regarding its corporate structure, financial standing (audited financial statement of the
past 3 years), proposed business plan, organizational setup, key personnels, risk
management framework, and such other information as may be sought by the Authority.

(4) An application which is incomplete shall not be processed.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: No person may act as a Pension Fund without a certificate of registration from the Authority. Applications are made through SWIT with the specified fee and documents, and the applicant must provide comprehensive details — corporate structure, three years' audited financials, business plan, organisational setup, key personnel and risk-management framework. An incomplete application is not processed.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Registration is the gateway, and the 'not processed if incomplete' rule means the SWIT filing has to be complete on submission — a thin application does not start the clock, it simply sits. Assemble the three-year audited financials and the risk-management framework before filing, not after a deficiency letter.
regulation_content.practical_point: Build the application pack to the Regulation 4(3) checklist before filing on SWIT; a missing limb means no processing at all, not a curable deficiency.
regulation_content.compliance_point: File a complete SWIT application with fee and all Regulation 4(3) particulars; retain the acknowledgement.
regulation_content.risk_point: Filing an incomplete application to 'hold a place' achieves nothing here — it is simply not processed, and the time is lost.
regulation_content.interview_point: An interviewer may ask what must accompany a Pension Fund registration application and what happens to an incomplete one.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Application via SWIT; 3 years' audited financials required; incomplete application not processed
regulation_content.applicability: All applicants for Pension Fund registration

regulation_content.chapter_title: Registration And Eligibility Of Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
5. Eligibility for Registration

(1) The applicant shall be an entity incorporated as a company in the International
Financial Services Centre, or a branch of a company incorporated outside the
International Financial Services Centre:

Provided that the branch structure is permitted only for a Pension Fund which is already
registered or regulated by a financial sector regulator in India or a foreign jurisdiction
for undertaking similar activities.

(2) The Board of the applicant shall consist of at least four directors, of whom at least
one-half shall be independent directors.

(3) The applicant and its promoters shall be from a jurisdiction which has not been
identified in the public statement of Financial Action Task Force (FATF) as “High-Risk
Jurisdictions subject to call for action”.

(4) The applicant or its parent or associate shall have experience in managing a pension
fund, retail fund, insurance business, or commercial bank for a minimum period of ten
(10) years.

Explanation.- For the purposes of this sub-regulation, “associate” shall, in relation to a
person, means another person who exercises control over at least fifty per cent of the
total voting power of the first person.

(5) The applicant shall maintain a minimum net worth of USD 1 million at all times:

Provided that where the applicant is a parent entity, the minimum net worth shall be
maintained at the parent level.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the eligibility conditions. The applicant must be a company incorporated in the IFSC, or a branch of a company incorporated outside the IFSC (the branch route only for a pension fund already registered/regulated by a financial-sector regulator in India or abroad for similar activity). The Board must have at least four directors, at least half of them independent. The applicant and promoters must be from a jurisdiction not on the FATF 'high-risk / call for action' list. The applicant, its parent or an associate must have at least ten years' experience managing a pension fund, retail fund, insurance business or commercial bank. A minimum net worth of USD 1 million must be maintained at all times (at parent level where the applicant is a parent entity).
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Four gates operate together, and two are easy to under-plan. The ten-year track record can be met at parent or associate level — 'associate' here means control of at least 50% of voting power — so a new IFSC entity can lean on a qualifying group entity. And the USD 1 million net worth is an at-all-times condition, not a one-time entry test, so a mid-year erosion is a breach even if later restored. The board-independence requirement (half of at least four) is a governance condition that has to hold continuously.
regulation_content.practical_point: Confirm which group entity supplies the ten-year experience and document the 50%-control associate link. Stand up the four-director board with at least half independent before filing, and build a rolling net-worth monitor rather than an annual check.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain net worth of USD 1 million at all times (parent level for a parent applicant); keep the board at >=4 directors with >=1/2 independent; retain evidence of the ten-year track record and FATF-jurisdiction status.
regulation_content.example: A newly incorporated IFSC pension fund whose parent has run a retail fund for twelve years meets the experience test through the parent; it must still hold USD 1 million net worth and seat a four-member board with two independents.
regulation_content.risk_point: Net-worth erosion between reporting dates and a lapse in board independence (for example, an independent director resigning and not being promptly replaced) are the recurring continuing-eligibility breaches an inspection will test.
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to state the four eligibility gates and explain that the ten-year experience can sit at parent/associate level while the USD 1 million net worth is a continuing, at-all-times requirement.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Company in IFSC or branch (branch only if already regulated); board >=4 directors, >=1/2 independent; 10 years' experience (parent/associate, associate = 50% voting control); net worth USD 1 million at all times

regulation_content.chapter_title: Registration And Eligibility Of Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
6. Appointment of Key Managerial Personnel(s)

(1) The applicant shall appoint a minimum of two Key Managerial Personnels who shall
be responsible for the activities of the Pension Fund, including but not limited to, fund
management, risk management, etc.

(2) The Pension Fund shall additionally appoint a Compliance Officer who shall be a
Key Managerial Personnel for overall compliance of these regulations and other
applicable laws and he shall report directly to the Board.

(3) The employees appointed in accordance with sub-regulation (1) and (2) shall have:

 (a) a post-graduate degree or post graduate diploma (minimum one year in
 duration) in finance, law, accountancy, business management, commerce,
 economics, capital market, banking, insurance or actuarial science from a
 university or an institution recognised by the Central Government or any State
 Government or a recognised foreign university or institution or association; or
 professional qualification such as Chartered Financial Analyst or a Financial
 Risk Manager from Global Association of Risk Professionals, or equivalent;
 and

 (b) minimum three (3) years of work experience in pension sector, fund
 management, fund operations, investment banking, or asset management,
 involving direct responsibility for managing financial assets or overseeing
 critical fund operations.

Provided that a bachelor's degree in finance, law, accountancy, business management,
commerce, or economics shall also suffice for a person with more than ten (10) years of
work experience in pension sector, fund management, fund operations, investment
banking or asset management.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the applicant to appoint at least two Key Managerial Personnel responsible for the Pension Fund's activities (including fund and risk management), plus a Compliance Officer who is a KMP responsible for overall compliance and who reports directly to the Board. All such personnel must hold a post-graduate degree/diploma (minimum one year) in a relevant discipline — or a professional qualification such as CFA or FRM — together with at least three years' relevant experience; a bachelor's degree suffices where the person has more than ten years' experience.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The Compliance Officer's direct line to the Board is a deliberate independence feature — it should not be diluted by routing the role through the CEO. The qualification test is a genuine screen: the three-year floor rises to a bachelor-plus-ten-years alternative, so onboarding files need to evidence both the qualification and the experience limb.
regulation_content.practical_point: Fix the two KMPs and the Compliance Officer before the fund goes live, and keep the Compliance Officer's Board reporting line explicit in the org chart. Hold qualification and experience evidence on file for each.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Appoint >=2 KMPs and a Compliance Officer (reporting directly to the Board); retain evidence that each meets the qualification-and-experience criteria.
regulation_content.risk_point: A Compliance Officer reporting into management rather than the Board undercuts the independence the regulation intends, and is an obvious governance finding.
regulation_content.interview_point: The interviewer may test the minimum KMP structure and why the Compliance Officer reports directly to the Board.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Min 2 KMPs + Compliance Officer (reports directly to Board); PG degree/diploma or CFA/FRM + 3 yrs; bachelor + 10 yrs alternative

regulation_content.chapter_title: Registration And Eligibility Of Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
7. Fit and proper requirements

(1) A Pension Fund shall ensure that all its director(s), Key Managerial Personnel(s) and
controlling shareholders are ‘fit and proper’ persons at all times, as per the criteria
specified in the First Schedule.

(2) Any person who has been declared not to be a ‘fit and proper’ person by an order of
a regulatory authority shall not be eligible to seek registration, or be a director, Key
Managerial Personnel, or controlling shareholder, as the case may be, until such person
satisfies the ‘fit and proper’ criteria of the said regulatory authority.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the Pension Fund to ensure that all its directors, KMPs and controlling shareholders are 'fit and proper' at all times, per the First Schedule criteria. A person declared not fit and proper by a regulator's order is ineligible to seek registration or to be a director, KMP or controlling shareholder until they satisfy that regulator's fit-and-proper criteria.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: 'Fit and proper at all times' makes this a continuing screen, not a one-off at appointment — a subsequent disqualifying event (see the First Schedule list) has to be caught and acted on. The cross-regulator bar means a person disqualified elsewhere cannot simply move into an IFSC pension fund role.
regulation_content.practical_point: Run First Schedule fit-and-proper checks at appointment and refresh them periodically, and build a self-declaration/monitoring process for disqualifying events across the board, KMPs and controlling shareholders.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain current fit-and-proper records for all directors, KMPs and controlling shareholders against the First Schedule; act promptly on any disqualifying event.
regulation_content.risk_point: Treating fit-and-proper as a one-time check misses later disqualifications — an unresolved economic-offence charge-sheet or a regulatory debarment against a KMP is exactly what the continuing test is meant to surface.
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to explain that fit-and-proper is a continuing, all-times requirement and cite the kinds of disqualification in the First Schedule.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Directors, KMPs and controlling shareholders fit and proper at all times (First Schedule)

regulation_content.chapter_title: Registration And Eligibility Of Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
8. Furnishing of information

(1) The Authority may require the applicant to furnish any additional information or
clarification for considering the application.

(2) While considering an application, the Authority may also require the applicant to
appear before it for personal representation or clarification.

 [भाग III—खण्‍ड 4] भारत‍का‍राजपत्र‍:‍असाधारण 37

 (3) The Authority may also undertake inspection of the applicant’s office prior to the
 grant of certificate of registration.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives the Authority flexibility to seek further information, personal representation and even a pre-registration office inspection.

regulation_content.chapter_title: Registration And Eligibility Of Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
9. Grant of registration

 (1) The Authority, upon being satisfied that the applicant fulfils the eligibility criteria and
 requirements specified in these regulations, may grant a certificate of registration as a
 Pension Fund, subject to the payment of the applicable fee.

 (2) The grant of registration may be subject to such terms and conditions as the Authority
 deems fit, including, but not limited to, compliance with specific operational or financial
 requirements.

 (3) If the Authority, upon the examination of the application, is of the opinion that the
 registration cannot be granted, it shall communicate the deficiencies to the applicant,
 giving it thirty (30) days’ time to rectify them.

 (4) If the Applicant fails to rectify such deficiencies to the satisfaction of the Authority
 within the specified time, the Authority may dispose of the application and shall
 communicate the same to the Applicant, with reasons thereof.

 (5) The certificate of registration granted to a Pension Fund shall be valid unless it is
 suspended or cancelled by the Authority or voluntarily surrendered by the Pension Fund:

 Provided that the voluntary surrender of certificate of registration shall be effective only
 after its acceptance by the Authority.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: On being satisfied that the applicant meets the eligibility criteria, the Authority may grant registration subject to the applicable fee and to such terms and conditions (including operational or financial conditions) as it deems fit. Deficiencies carry a thirty-day cure period; failure to cure lets the Authority dispose of the application with reasons. A certificate stays valid until suspended, cancelled or voluntarily surrendered — and a voluntary surrender is effective only once the Authority accepts it.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Registration is open-ended (no fixed renewal), so the weight sits on continuing compliance with the attached conditions. The surrender-needs-acceptance rule means a fund cannot walk away unilaterally — exit runs through the Authority.
regulation_content.practical_point: Track every condition attached to the certificate on an ongoing basis; for an exit, plan for Authority acceptance of the surrender rather than a self-determined closure date.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Comply with all conditions of registration continuously; respond to any deficiency letter within thirty days; route any surrender for Authority acceptance.
regulation_content.important_numbers: 30 days to cure deficiencies; registration valid until suspended/cancelled/surrendered; surrender effective only on Authority acceptance

regulation_content.chapter_title: Registration And Eligibility Of Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
10. Ongoing compliance

 A Pension Fund shall, at all times:

(a) maintain a fully functional office within the International Financial Service Centre,
 which is adequate for its current and projected operations, including investment
 management, risk management, compliance, and administrative functions, and such
 office shall be equipped with necessary infrastructure, including but not limited to, a
 secure information technology system, communication facilities and data storage
 capabilities;

 Explanation - the information technology system deployed by a Pension Fund
 covering all aspects of its operations, including investment analysis, trading, risk
 monitoring, valuation, record-keeping, and cyber security;
(b) develop and implement comprehensive internal policies and procedures covering all
 aspects of its operations, including investment decision-making, risk management,
 compliance, grievance redressal, which policies and procedures shall be regularly
 reviewed and updated;
(c) comply with the International Financial Services Centre Authority (AML/CFT/KYC)
 Guidelines, 2022, as amended from time to time;
(d) establish a clear organizational structure with well-defined roles, responsibilities, and
 reporting lines for ensuring adequate segregation of duties; and
(e) ensure continual compliance with all provisions of the Act, these regulations, and
 relevant subsidiary instruction as issued by the Authority from time to time, as well
 as other applicable laws.

 CHAPTER III
 SCHEME FEATURES
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the continuing-compliance baseline. At all times the Pension Fund must maintain a fully functional IFSC office adequate for current and projected operations (with secure IT, communications and data-storage infrastructure); develop and regularly update comprehensive internal policies covering investment, risk, compliance and grievance redressal; comply with the IFSCA AML/CFT/KYC Guidelines, 2022; maintain a clear organisational structure with segregation of duties; and ensure continual compliance with the Act, these Regulations and subsidiary instructions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is the always-on operating standard that underpins the specific obligations — a real IFSC office and a live, updated policy suite, not a paper presence. It reads directly into the default provision (Regulation 42), so a hollow office or stale policies is a registration-condition failure.
regulation_content.practical_point: Stand up a genuine IFSC office with the required IT/data infrastructure and a policy suite that is reviewed and version-controlled, not drafted once and shelved.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain a functional IFSC office and current internal policies; comply with the AML/CFT/KYC Guidelines, 2022; keep documented segregation of duties.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Functional IFSC office; regularly updated internal policies; AML/CFT/KYC Guidelines, 2022; segregation of duties

regulation_content.regulation_text:
11. Contribution structure

(1) A Pension Fund shall provide Subscribers with the flexibility to determine the
frequency and amount of their contributions.

(2) A Pension Fund may fix a minimum contribution amount, with the prior approval of
the Authority.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Allows Subscribers flexibility over the frequency and amount of contributions. A minimum contribution may be fixed only with prior approval of the Authority.

regulation_content.regulation_text:
12 Investment options and Scheme types

(1) Pension Fund may offer a range of investment options, including:

 (a) Active choice: Subscribers may actively choose their asset allocation across
 various asset classes within the specified limit; and
 (b) Auto choice (life cycle fund): A default option where asset allocation changes
 automatically based on the Subscriber's age, gradually shifting from aggressive to
 conservative, as they approach retirement.
(2) Each Scheme shall have a clearly defined investment objective, strategy and risk
profile, which shall be detailed in its Scheme Information Document.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Recognises active-choice and auto-choice/life-cycle investment options. Every Scheme must have a defined investment objective, strategy and risk profile disclosed in its Scheme Information Document.

regulation_content.regulation_text:
13. Scheme filing and approval process

(1) Each Scheme offered by a Pension Fund shall be constituted as a trust.

(2) A Pension Fund shall seek prior approval of the Authority for each new Scheme, or
any material modification proposed to be made to an existing Scheme, as the case may
be, by filing requisite details with the Authority.

(3) The filing referred to in sub-regulation (2) shall, inter alia, include the Scheme
Information Document and such other information as may be required by the Authority.

(4) A Pension Fund shall appoint a Trustee prior to filing the Scheme Information
Document with the Authority and shall ensure that the Trustee meets with the ‘fit and
proper’ requirements as specified in the First Schedule.

(5) The scheme, as approved by the Authority, shall be launched within a period of twelve
(12) months from the date of communication of such approval.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Each Scheme must be constituted as a trust. The Pension Fund must obtain the Authority's prior approval for every new Scheme and for any material modification to an existing one, filing the Scheme Information Document and required details. A Trustee (meeting the First Schedule fit-and-proper criteria) must be appointed before the SID is filed. An approved Scheme must be launched within twelve months of the approval communication.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The sequencing is prescriptive and easy to get wrong: appoint the Trustee first, then file the SID, then obtain approval, then launch within twelve months. A material modification to a live Scheme is itself a prior-approval event, so scheme changes cannot be made administratively.
regulation_content.practical_point: Run the Scheme launch as a gated sequence — Trustee appointment, SID filing, Authority approval, launch within twelve months — and treat any material change to a running Scheme as a fresh prior-approval filing.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Appoint a fit-and-proper Trustee before filing the SID; obtain prior approval for each new Scheme or material modification; launch within twelve months of approval.
regulation_content.example: A Pension Fund approving a new life-cycle Scheme on 1 April must appoint the Trustee and file the SID beforehand, and launch the Scheme by the following 31 March.
regulation_content.risk_point: Filing the SID before the Trustee is appointed, or making a material change to a live Scheme without prior approval, are the sequencing breaches; missing the twelve-month launch window lapses the approval.
regulation_content.interview_point: A practical question: put the steps for launching a pension Scheme in order, and state the launch deadline after approval.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Scheme = trust; prior approval for new Scheme/material modification; Trustee appointed before SID filing; launch within 12 months of approval

regulation_content.regulation_text:
14. Withdrawal and exit options

(1) The withdrawal and exit options available to a Subscriber under a Scheme shall be
as under:

 (a) Provision for partial withdrawal (Pre-retirement): Limited partial
 withdrawals may be permitted for higher education, marriage, critical illness,
 housing, or any other purposes as maybe specified by the Authority, after
 completion of a minimum lock-in period of five years:

[भाग III—खण्‍ड 4] भारत‍का‍राजपत्र‍:‍असाधारण 39

 Provided that the amount of partial withdrawal shall not exceed seventy-five
 percent of Subscriber’s contribution, or such lower limit as may be disclosed in
 the Scheme Information Document:

 Provided further that in case of withdrawal on account of critical illness, such
 partial withdrawal may be permitted without any minimum lock-in period.

 (b) At retirement/superannuation/vesting period: Upon contributing for a
 minimum of ten years or upon attaining the age of superannuation, that is sixty
 years, whichever is earlier, a Subscriber intending to exit the scheme shall opt
 for a Systematic Withdrawal Plan:

 Provided that in case of attainment of age of superannuation, the Subscriber
 may defer the withdrawal of the accumulated corpus, with or without further
 contributions, till he attains the age of seventy-five years.

(2) The withdrawal of corpus under clause (b) of sub-regulation (1) shall be subject to a
minimum of twenty per cent. of the total accumulated corpus through a Systematic
Withdrawal Plan and balance be payable lump sum to the Subscriber:

Provided that where a total accumulated corpus of a Subscriber is below a threshold
specified by the Authority, the entire amount may be withdrawn as a lump sum upon
retirement/superannuation.

(3) If a Subscriber exits from the Scheme before superannuation or vesting period, a
minimum of twenty-five per cent. of the total corpus shall be utilised by the Subscriber
for the Systematic Withdrawal Plan and the remaining of the corpus maybe withdrawn
as lumpsum, subject to the threshold referred to in sub-regulation (2).

(4) In the event of the Subscriber's death, the entire accumulated corpus shall be paid as
a lump sum to the nominee(s), or, in his absence, to the legal heir(s).
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the withdrawal and exit regime. Pre-retirement partial withdrawal is allowed only after a five-year lock-in, capped at 75% of the subscriber's contribution (or a lower SID limit) and for specified purposes (higher education, marriage, critical illness, housing, etc.) — with the lock-in waived for critical illness. At retirement/superannuation (age sixty) or after contributing for at least ten years, whichever is earlier, the subscriber exits via a Systematic Withdrawal Plan, and may defer withdrawal (with or without further contributions) up to age seventy-five. At least 20% of the accumulated corpus must go through the SWP with the balance payable lump sum (full lump sum allowed below an Authority-specified threshold). On early exit before superannuation/vesting, at least 25% must go through the SWP. On the subscriber's death, the entire corpus is paid lump sum to the nominee or legal heir.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is the most number-dense provision in the framework and the one subscribers ask about most, so the figures have to be exact. Two distinctions matter: the partial-withdrawal cap is 75% of contribution (not of corpus), and the mandatory-SWP proportion differs by exit route — 20% at normal retirement versus 25% on early exit. The critical-illness waiver of the five-year lock-in is the humane exception built into an otherwise firm lock-in.
regulation_content.practical_point: Map each withdrawal request to the correct route and test it against the right figure — 75% of contribution for a partial withdrawal, 20% SWP at retirement, 25% SWP on early exit — and check the five-year lock-in (waived only for critical illness).
regulation_content.compliance_point: Enforce the five-year lock-in (except critical illness), the 75%-of-contribution partial cap, and the 20%/25% minimum SWP proportions by exit route; pay the full corpus lump sum to nominee/legal heir on death.
regulation_content.example: A subscriber taking a partial withdrawal in year six for housing can draw up to 75% of contributions; at superannuation, at least 20% of the corpus must fund a SWP with the rest paid lump sum; on early exit at year eight, at least 25% must fund the SWP.
regulation_content.risk_point: Applying the 75% cap to corpus instead of contribution, or the 20% SWP proportion to an early exit that requires 25%, are the recurring miscalculations — each is a quantifiable breach against the subscriber's account.
regulation_content.interview_point: The interviewer may test the exact figures: partial-withdrawal cap and lock-in, superannuation age, minimum contribution years, and the different SWP proportions for normal versus early exit.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Partial withdrawal: after 5-yr lock-in, <=75% of contribution (critical-illness: no lock-in). Exit at age 60 or 10 yrs' contribution; SWP >=20% of corpus at retirement; >=25% on early exit; defer up to age 75; death: full corpus lump sum to nominee/heir
regulation_content.applicability: All Pension Fund Schemes and subscribers

regulation_content.regulation_text:
15. Portability

(1) A Subscriber shall have the right to change the Pension Fund up to a maximum of
two (2) times per Financial Year.

(2) The Authority may specify the mechanism for interoperability with other pension
systems, subject to bilateral agreements and applicable regulatory approvals.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives a subscriber the right to change the Pension Fund up to twice per financial year. The Authority may specify a mechanism for interoperability with other pension systems, subject to bilateral agreements and applicable approvals.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Portability: max 2 changes of Pension Fund per financial year

regulation_content.regulation_text:
16. Nomination

A Subscriber shall have the right to nominate one or more persons, or change such
nomination(s), who shall receive the accumulated corpus in the event of his death.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives Subscribers the right to nominate one or more persons and to change their nominations for receipt of accumulated corpus on death.

regulation_content.regulation_text:
17. Healthcare benefit option

(1) A Pension Fund may also offer a healthcare benefit option that allows Subscriber to
allocate a portion of his pension contribution towards a dedicated healthcare savings
account, information about which shall be included in Scheme Information Document.

(2) The healthcare benefit option offered in a Scheme by the Pension Fund shall comply
with the requirements specified in the Second Schedule.

 CHAPTER IV
 INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT AND ASSET ALLOCATION
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets a Pension Fund offer a healthcare benefit option under which a subscriber allocates part of the pension contribution to a dedicated healthcare savings account, with details in the SID. The option must comply with the Second Schedule.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The healthcare option is bounded by the Second Schedule — a separate sub-account, prior Authority approval, a voluntary basis and a 10%-of-contribution cap. It is a distinct feature to be enabled deliberately, not a default.
regulation_content.practical_point: If offering the option, obtain prior Authority approval, ring-fence the healthcare sub-account and cap allocations at 10% of contributions per the Second Schedule.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain a separate healthcare sub-account; obtain prior approval; keep allocations within the 10% cap (Second Schedule).
regulation_content.important_numbers: Healthcare option: separate sub-account; prior approval; <=10% of contributions (Second Schedule)
regulation_content.applicability: Pension Funds offering the healthcare option

regulation_content.regulation_text:
18. General principles of investment

The general principles of investment to be adhered to by a Pension Fund shall, inter-alia,
include the following:

 (a) Long-term investment horizon: The investment strategy shall be aligned with
 the long-term nature of pension liabilities.
 (b) Diversification: Investments shall be diversified across asset classes, sectors,
 and geographies, so as to reduce risk.
 (c) Liquidity: Sufficient liquidity shall be maintained to meet regular withdrawals
 and payments.
 (d) Risk management: A robust risk management framework shall be established
 to underpin all investment decisions.
 (e) Safety and prudence: The primary goal of investment shall be the long-term
 safety of the Scheme .
 (f) Stewardship: A Pension Fund shall act as a responsible steward of the assets of
 the Subscriber.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the investment principles around long-term horizon, diversification, liquidity, risk management, safety and stewardship of Subscriber assets.

regulation_content.regulation_text:
19. Permissible investments and limits

(1) A Pension Fund shall invest in any of the following asset classes:

 (a) listed public and private equities;
 (b) Fixed income instruments, such as government bonds, corporate bonds, private
 debt;
 (c) Alternative Investment Funds;
 (d) Frequently traded commodities;
 (e) Cash and short-term instruments for liquidity management; or
 (f) Such other financial products or instruments, as may be specified by the
 Authority.
(2) The specific investment limits for each class and sub-class of assets shall be in
accordance with the Part-A of Third Schedule titled “Permissible investments and
limits”.

(3) The specific investment limits for each class and sub-class of assets for a Scheme
shall be determined by the Pension Fund in accordance with sub-regulation (2) and the
same shall also be detailed in the respective Scheme Information Document.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the permissible asset classes for a Pension Fund — listed public and private equities; fixed income (government bonds, corporate bonds, private debt); Alternative Investment Funds; frequently traded commodities; cash and short-term instruments for liquidity; and other instruments the Authority specifies. The specific class and sub-class limits are in Part A of the Third Schedule and must also be detailed in each Scheme Information Document.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This provision sets the universe; the Third Schedule Part A sets the ceilings. The two must be read together, and the Scheme-level limits in the SID cannot be looser than the Third Schedule caps.
regulation_content.practical_point: Build the Scheme's asset-allocation ranges off the Third Schedule Part A caps and mirror them in the SID; monitor exposures against both the class and sub-class limits.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Invest only in the permitted asset classes; keep Scheme allocations within the Third Schedule Part A limits and disclose them in the SID.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Permitted: equities, fixed income, AIFs, frequently traded commodities, cash/short-term. Limits per Third Schedule Part A
regulation_content.related_provisions: Regulation 20; Regulation 21; Third Schedule Part A

regulation_content.regulation_text:
20. Geographic diversification

A Pension Fund shall adhere to the following exposure limits for investments in India
and global markets:

 (a) Exposure in India: Investment in assets, across all permissible asset classes,
 in India may be up to hundred per cent. (100%) of the Scheme's Assets under
 Management (AUM).

[भाग III—खण्‍ड 4] भारत‍का‍राजपत्र‍:‍असाधारण 41

 (b) Global market exposure (outside India): Investment in assets, across all
 permissible asset classes, in any one country shall not exceed twenty per cent.
 (20%) of the Scheme's Assets under Management (AUM), except in case of
 United States of America where the maximum limit shall be fifty per cent.
 (50%):

Explanation.- For the purpose of this regulation, the exposure limit shall include both
direct and indirect investments.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets geographic diversification limits. Investment in India, across all permissible asset classes, may be up to 100% of the Scheme's AUM. Investment in any single country outside India must not exceed 20% of AUM, except the United States, where the ceiling is 50%. The limits include both direct and indirect exposure.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The per-country ceiling is the control that prevents concentration in any one foreign market, with the US carve-out reflecting its market depth. The direct-and-indirect point is the trap — exposure through funds or ETFs counts towards the 20%/50% country limit, so look through to the underlying geography.
regulation_content.practical_point: Track country exposure on a look-through basis (direct plus indirect) and monitor each foreign country against 20%, with the US against 50%.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Keep single-country foreign exposure <= 20% of AUM (US <= 50%), counting direct and indirect holdings; India may be up to 100%.
regulation_content.example: A Scheme may hold up to 50% of AUM in US assets but no more than 20% in any other single foreign country; exposure taken through a US-focused ETF counts towards the US limit.
regulation_content.risk_point: Ignoring indirect exposure — treating a fund or ETF as country-neutral — is the common breach; the limit expressly captures indirect investment.
regulation_content.interview_point: A practical question: what is the maximum a pension Scheme can invest in a single foreign country, what is special about the US, and does exposure through an ETF count?
regulation_content.important_numbers: India up to 100% of AUM; any single foreign country <= 20%; USA <= 50%; includes direct + indirect exposure

regulation_content.regulation_text:
21. Concentration limits

Pension Fund shall adhere to concentration limits pertaining to single issuer and
counterparty, as specified in the Part-B of the Third Schedule.

 CHAPTER V
 RISK MANAGEMENT
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires adherence to the single-issuer and counterparty concentration limits in Part B of the Third Schedule.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The concentration limits are where issuer- and group-level risk is contained; the single-issuer 10% cap (with a government-securities exception) is the headline, alongside the sponsor/non-sponsor group and industry limits.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Monitor single-issuer, sponsor/non-sponsor group, industry and term-deposit exposures against the Third Schedule Part B limits.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Single issuer <= 10% (ex-government securities); sponsor group debt <= 5%; non-sponsor group debt <= 10%; industry <= 15%; term deposit <= 10% per bank (Third Schedule Part B)

regulation_content.regulation_text:
22. Enterprise-wide risk management

(1) Every Pension Fund shall establish and maintain a comprehensive enterprise-wide
risk management framework, approved by its Board, to identify, measure, monitor, and
mitigate all material risks arising from and associated with the management of the
Scheme.

(2) The framework referred to in sub-regulation (1) shall be integrated into all aspects of
the Pension Fund’s operations.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires every Pension Fund to establish and maintain a comprehensive, Board-approved enterprise-wide risk management framework to identify, measure, monitor and mitigate all material risks from managing the Scheme, integrated into all aspects of operations.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The ERM framework is Board-owned and enterprise-wide by design — it cannot be a siloed investment-desk exercise. The detail of the risk categories and methodologies is pushed to the Fourth Schedule and the fund's internal policies.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain a Board-approved ERM framework integrated across operations; evidence Board approval and periodic review.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Board-approved enterprise-wide risk management framework, integrated into all operations

regulation_content.regulation_text:
23. Key risk categories

(1) The risk management framework established by a Pension Fund shall, inter alia,
cover key risk categories as specified in the Fourth Schedule, and the detailed
methodologies for managing such risks shall be outlined in the Pension Fund’s internal
risk management policies in accordance with the requirements stipulated therein.

(2) A Pension Fund shall implement a currency risk management policy, which shall,
where appropriate, include hedging strategies.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the risk framework to cover the key risk categories specified in the Fourth Schedule, with detailed management methodologies in the fund's internal risk policies, and requires a currency risk management policy that includes hedging strategies where appropriate.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Fourth Schedule risk categories; currency risk policy with hedging where appropriate

regulation_content.regulation_text:
24. Risk appetite and limits

(1) The Board shall formulate and periodically review a comprehensive well-
documented risk appetite statement specifying the overall level of risk a Pension Fund is
willing to assume in the management of Scheme.

(2) The risk appetite statement shall be appropriately translated and operationalised into
specific, measurable and actionable quantitative and qualitative risk limits for the whole
portfolio as well as its individual components.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the Board to formulate and periodically review a documented risk appetite statement setting the overall level of risk the fund will assume, translated into specific, measurable and actionable quantitative and qualitative risk limits for the whole portfolio and its components.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The value is in the translation step — a risk appetite statement that is not converted into concrete portfolio and component limits is not operational. That conversion is what a reviewer will look for.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain a Board-reviewed risk appetite statement operationalised into measurable portfolio and component-level limits.

regulation_content.regulation_text:
25. Risk governance and oversight

(1) A Pension Fund shall implement a robust risk governance structure including a
dedicated Risk Committee at the Board level, with clearly defined roles and clear lines
of accountability.

(2) For the purpose of effective risk management, a Pension Fund shall adopt and
implement the three lines of defence model.

Explanation. - For the purpose of this regulation, the ‘three lines of defence’ shall
comprise of the following:

 (a) First line of defense (risk ownership): The investment management and the
 operations functions shall constitute the first line of defense which shall be
 primarily responsible for the day-to-day identification, assessment, ownership
 and control of all risks inherent in their activities, ensuring strict adherence to
 the Scheme's investment mandates and prudential norms.
 (b) Second line of defense (risk control): The compliance, legal and risk
 management functions shall constitute the second line of defense which shall
 be responsible for defining the overall risk appetite, establishing internal control
 policies, independently monitoring adherence to regulatory requirements and
 risk limits, and reporting any deficiencies to Board and the Trustee.
 (c) Third line of defense (independent assurance): The internal audit function,
 which must directly report to the Board, shall constitute the third line of defense
 providing objective and independent assurance to the Trustee and the Authority
 on the effectiveness of the governance, risk management processes and internal
 controls implemented by the first and second lines of defense.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires a robust risk governance structure with a dedicated Board-level Risk Committee and clear accountability, and adoption of the 'three lines of defence' model — first line (investment/operations owning day-to-day risk), second line (compliance, legal and risk defining appetite and independently monitoring limits, reporting deficiencies to the Board and Trustee), and third line (internal audit reporting directly to the Board, giving independent assurance to the Trustee and Authority).
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The three-lines model is prescribed, not optional, and the reporting lines are the substance — internal audit reports directly to the Board, and the second line reports deficiencies to both the Board and the Trustee. Blurring these lines (for example, letting the risk owner also assure the control) defeats the model.
regulation_content.practical_point: Stand up a Board-level Risk Committee and map roles to the three lines, keeping internal audit's direct-to-Board reporting and the second line's Board-and-Trustee reporting explicit.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Operate a Board-level Risk Committee and the three-lines-of-defence model with the prescribed reporting lines (internal audit direct to Board).
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to explain the three-lines-of-defence model and who each line reports to under these Regulations.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Board-level Risk Committee; three lines of defence (internal audit reports directly to Board)

regulation_content.regulation_text:
26. Stress testing and contingency planning

(1) A Pension Fund shall conduct comprehensive stress tests and scenario analyses at
regular intervals, to evaluate the resilience of the portfolio under extreme conditions.

(2) A Pension Fund shall formulate, implement and maintain robust business continuity
plans (BCP) and disaster recovery plans (DRP), which shall be regularly tested to ensure
uninterrupted operations.

 CHAPTER VI
 GENERAL OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the Pension Fund to conduct comprehensive stress tests and scenario analyses at regular intervals to evaluate portfolio resilience under extreme conditions, and to formulate, implement, maintain and regularly test business continuity (BCP) and disaster recovery (DRP) plans for uninterrupted operations.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Run regular stress tests and scenario analyses; maintain and periodically test BCP and DRP.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Regular stress testing and scenario analysis; tested BCP and DRP

regulation_content.regulation_text:
27. Record-keeping and administration

(1) A Pension Fund shall maintain a comprehensive, secure and electronic record-
keeping system for all Subscriber’s data and transactions, and ensure the integrity,
confidentiality and availability of such data at all times, is in accordance with the
applicable laws.

(2) Each Subscriber shall be assigned a unique Pension Account number by the Pension
Fund.

(3) A Pension Fund shall provide Subscriber with online access to his Pension Account
details including transaction history, current valuation and investment allocation.

[भाग III—खण्‍ड 4] भारत‍का‍राजपत्र‍:‍असाधारण 43
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires a comprehensive, secure, electronic record-keeping system for all subscriber data and transactions (with integrity, confidentiality and availability maintained at all times), a unique Pension Account number for each subscriber, and online access for subscribers to their account details including transaction history, current valuation and investment allocation.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain secure electronic records with subscriber online access; assign a unique Pension Account number to each subscriber.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Secure electronic records; unique Pension Account number; subscriber online access

regulation_content.regulation_text:
28. Reporting and disclosures

(1) A Pension Fund shall submit report about its operations, financial performance,
investment portfolios, compliance status, and any other information, in such form and
manner and within such timelines (including monthly, quarterly, and annually) as may
be specified by the Authority.

(2) A Pension Fund shall, while onboarding a Subscriber, disclose the following :

 (a) Scheme Information Document;
 (b) Fees and charges;
 (c) Grievance redressal procedures;
 (d) Terms and conditions for contributions, withdrawals, and exit;
 (e) Performance reports, on a yearly basis; and
 (f) Annual consolidated statements detailing all transactions, investment
 performance, and fees charged.

(3) Any subsequent changes in the details furnished under clauses (a) to (d) of sub-
regulation (2) shall be immediately disclosed to the Subscribers.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires reporting to the Authority on operations, financial performance, investment portfolios and compliance in the specified form and timelines (monthly, quarterly and annually), and, at subscriber onboarding, disclosure of the SID, fees and charges, grievance-redressal procedures, contribution/withdrawal/exit terms, annual performance reports and annual consolidated statements; subsequent changes to the onboarding disclosures must be disclosed to subscribers immediately.
regulation_content.compliance_point: File monthly/quarterly/annual reports as specified; make the full onboarding disclosures and update subscribers immediately on any change to SID, fees, grievance or terms.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Reporting monthly/quarterly/annually; onboarding disclosures; immediate disclosure of changes

regulation_content.regulation_text:
29. Grievance redressal mechanism

A Pension Fund shall take adequate steps for redressal of grievances of the Subscriber in
accordance with the circular titled “Complaint Handling and Grievance Redressal by
Regulated Entities in the IFSC” dated December 02, 2024, issued by the Authority.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires adequate grievance redressal in accordance with the Authority's circular 'Complaint Handling and Grievance Redressal by Regulated Entities in the IFSC' dated 2 December 2024.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Grievance redressal per IFSCA circular dated 2 December 2024

regulation_content.regulation_text:
30. Auditing requirements

(1) A Pension Fund shall undergo an annual financial audit conducted by an independent
auditor in accordance with the applicable laws, and the report of such audit shall be
submitted to the Authority within thirty (30) days from its receipt.

(2) The Authority may also conduct special audits or appoint auditors to undertake
concurrent audits, as deemed necessary.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires an annual financial audit by an independent auditor under applicable law, with the audit report submitted to the Authority within thirty days of its receipt; the Authority may also order special or concurrent audits.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The thirty-day clock runs from the fund's receipt of the audit report, not from the financial-year end, so diarise it off report receipt.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Have an independent auditor conduct the annual audit; submit the report to the Authority within thirty days of receiving it.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Annual independent audit; report to Authority within 30 days of receipt; special/concurrent audits possible

regulation_content.regulation_text:
31. Custody of assets

(1) A Pension Fund shall ensure that all assets of the Scheme are held in the safe custody
of a Custodian.

(2) The Custodian shall be independent of the Pension Fund and shall be responsible for
the safekeeping and settlement of Scheme assets, and reporting of holdings, in
accordance with applicable law and regulatory requirements.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires all Scheme assets to be held in the safe custody of a Custodian that is independent of the Pension Fund and responsible for safekeeping, settlement and reporting of holdings under applicable law.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Custodian independence is the asset-protection backbone — the entity that manages the Scheme cannot also hold its assets. Retain the custody agreement evidencing independence.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Appoint an independent Custodian for all Scheme assets; retain the custody agreement and holding reports.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Independent Custodian holds all Scheme assets

regulation_content.regulation_text:
32. Creation of the trust

(1) The trust under sub-regulation (1) of regulation 13 shall be settled under the
applicable laws in force in India.

(2) The trust deed shall also include roles and responsibilities of the Trustee in
accordance with the requirements specified under these regulations.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the Scheme trust (under Regulation 13(1)) to be settled under applicable Indian law, with the trust deed setting out the Trustee's roles and responsibilities as required by these Regulations.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Scheme trust settled under Indian law; trust deed sets Trustee roles

regulation_content.provision_heading: Eligibility for the appointment of Trustee
regulation_content.regulation_text:
33. Eligibility for the appointment of Trustee

The entity proposed to be appointed as Trustee shall meet the eligibility conditions as
follows:

 (a) it shall be independent of the Pension Fund ;
 (b) it shall be authorised/registered with the Authority or with any other financial
 sector regulator to act as a trustee; and
 (c) it shall have adequate infrastructure, manpower and other related wherewithal to
 the satisfaction of the Authority, to carry out its functions and obligations.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the eligibility for appointing a Trustee — it must be independent of the Pension Fund, authorised/registered with the Authority or another financial-sector regulator to act as trustee, and have adequate infrastructure, manpower and resources to the Authority's satisfaction.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Appoint a Trustee that is independent, regulator-authorised as a trustee, and adequately resourced; retain evidence of each.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Trustee: independent; regulator-authorised as trustee; adequately resourced

regulation_content.provision_heading: Roles and responsibilities of the Trustee
regulation_content.regulation_text:
34. Roles and responsibilities of the Trustee

(1) A Trustee, all its directors, officers and members of its governing body shall, at all
times, act in a fiduciary capacity for the benefit of the Subscribers, and shall manage and
administer the affairs of the Scheme solely in the interest of the Subscribers with the
objective of protecting and enhancing their superannuation benefits.

(2) A Trustee shall exercise its powers and carry out its duties with care, diligence, skill,
and prudence that a reasonable and prudent person would exercise in the conduct of a
similar enterprise, and shall comply with all provisions of these regulations, the trust
deed and other applicable laws.

(3) A Trustee shall ensure that in the event of a potential or actual conflict of interest, the
interests of the Subscribers shall take precedence over all other interests, including those
of the Trustee, Pension Fund or any related party.

(4) A Trustee shall be responsible for ensuring that the Scheme is administered in strict
compliance with the Scheme Information Document, these regulations, subsidiary
instruction issued by the Authority from time to time, and other applicable laws.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the Trustee's duties. The Trustee, its directors, officers and governing-body members must at all times act in a fiduciary capacity for the subscribers' benefit, manage the Scheme solely in their interest, exercise the care, diligence, skill and prudence of a reasonable and prudent person, give subscribers' interests precedence in any conflict, and ensure the Scheme is administered in strict compliance with the SID, these Regulations and subsidiary instructions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is a full fiduciary standard — the subscriber-first conflict rule is absolute, ahead of the interests of the Trustee, the Pension Fund and any related party. It is the governance counterweight to the Pension Fund's operational control.
regulation_content.practical_point: Ensure the trust deed embeds the fiduciary standard and the conflict-precedence rule, and that Trustee decision records show subscriber-interest primacy.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Operate the trust on a fiduciary, subscriber-first basis; document conflict management giving subscribers precedence.
regulation_content.risk_point: A Trustee decision that favours the Pension Fund or a related party over subscribers breaches the core fiduciary duty and is a serious governance failure.
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to describe the Trustee's fiduciary duty and how conflicts of interest must be resolved.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Trustee acts in fiduciary capacity; subscribers' interests take precedence in any conflict

regulation_content.regulation_text:
35. Engagement of Distributor

(1) A Pension Fund may engage one or more distributors for the purpose of marketing,
soliciting or servicing Subscribers.

(2) Notwithstanding the engagement referred to in sub-regulation (1), a Pension Fund
shall remain fully and solely responsible for the conduct, compliance and activities of
any distributor engaged, and shall ensure that such distributor adheres to these
regulations and any other directions issued by the Authority.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets a Pension Fund engage one or more distributors for marketing, solicitation or servicing, but the Pension Fund remains fully and solely responsible for the conduct, compliance and activities of any distributor engaged, and must ensure the distributor follows these Regulations and the Authority's directions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Delegation of distribution is not delegation of responsibility — the fund carries full liability for distributor conduct. Build oversight and contractual controls accordingly.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Retain full responsibility for distributor conduct; put oversight, training and contractual compliance controls in place.
regulation_content.risk_point: Assuming a distributor's mis-selling is the distributor's problem is the misconception this provision forecloses; the liability stays with the Pension Fund.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Distributor allowed; Pension Fund fully and solely responsible for distributor conduct

regulation_content.regulation_text:
36. Subscriber education and awareness

(1) A Pension Fund shall be responsible for promoting financial literacy among potential
Subscribers and providing timely, accurate and comprehensive information regarding the
operation of the scheme, the risks associated with various investment options, fee
structures and the subscriber's rights and responsibilities.

(2) A Pension Fund shall ensure that all key educational materials, performance
disclosures and details pertaining to the Scheme are made available to every Subscriber
in a readily accessible, clear and easy-to-understand format.

[भाग III—खण्‍ड 4] भारत‍का‍राजपत्र‍:‍असाधारण 45
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Makes the Pension Fund responsible for promoting financial literacy among potential subscribers and providing timely, accurate and comprehensive information on scheme operation, investment-option risks, fee structures and subscriber rights and responsibilities, in a readily accessible, clear and easy-to-understand format.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Subscriber education, risk/fee disclosure in clear accessible format

regulation_content.regulation_text:
37. Change in control

A Pension Fund shall seek prior approval of the Authority in case of any direct or indirect
change in its control:

Provided that where a Pension Fund operating in the form of a branch is required to take
prior approval from its sectoral regulator in its principal place of operation, it shall only
inform such change to the Authority, within fifteen (15) days thereof.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the Pension Fund to obtain the Authority's prior approval for any direct or indirect change in its control. Where a branch Pension Fund must obtain prior approval from its sectoral regulator at its principal place of operation, it instead informs the Authority within fifteen days of the change.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Prior approval for change in control is the norm; the fifteen-day intimation is the branch-specific alternative. Map the control chain so an indirect change (for example, at the parent) is caught before completion.
regulation_content.practical_point: Identify direct and indirect control changes early; route as prior-approval applications, or as a fifteen-day intimation for a qualifying branch.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Obtain prior approval for any direct/indirect change in control (branch: intimate within 15 days); document the control mapping.
regulation_content.risk_point: Completing a control change — including an indirect one at the parent — without prior approval is a serious breach.
regulation_content.interview_point: A practical question: does an indirect change of control need prior approval, and how is a branch Pension Fund treated?
regulation_content.important_numbers: Change in control: prior approval; branch: intimate within 15 days

regulation_content.regulation_text:
38. Payment of fees

A Pension Fund shall pay annual fees, Scheme Information Document filing fee, and any
other fees as may be specified by the Authority from time to time.

 CHAPTER VII
 FINANCIAL ASPECTS
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the Pension Fund to pay annual fees, the Scheme Information Document filing fee, and any other fees the Authority specifies.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Annual fee; SID filing fee; other specified fees

regulation_content.provision_heading: Fees and charges levied by a Pension Fund
regulation_content.regulation_text:
39. Fees and charges levied by a Pension Fund

(1) A Pension Fund shall take prior approval of the Authority to levy fees and charges on
the Subscribers.

(2) The charges mentioned under sub-regulation (1) may include account opening
charges, annual maintenance charges, investment management fees (as a percentage of
Assets under Management), and transaction charges.

(3) A Pension Fund shall disclose complete details of all fees and charges proposed to be
levied on the Subscribers, in the Scheme Information Document and other relevant
documents.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires prior Authority approval to levy fees and charges on subscribers (which may include account-opening, annual maintenance, investment-management (as a percentage of AUM) and transaction charges), with full disclosure of all proposed fees in the SID and other relevant documents.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Obtain prior approval before levying subscriber fees; disclose all fees fully in the SID.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Prior approval to levy subscriber fees; full fee disclosure in SID

regulation_content.provision_heading: Valuation and Net Asset Value calculation
regulation_content.regulation_text:
40. Valuation and Net Asset Value calculation

(1) Assets and liabilities of the Scheme shall be valued on daily basis, at market prices,
as per the methodologies fully disclosed and documented by the Pension Fund.

(2) The Net Asset Value (NAV) per unit for each Scheme shall be calculated and declared
daily, based on the total value of assets less liabilities, divided by the number of
outstanding units.

(3) For the purpose of carrying out valuation functions, a Pension Fund may appoint a
valuer registered with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India or the Authority, or
such other person as may be specified by the Authority.

 CHAPTER VIII
 COMPLIANCE AND ENFORCEMENT
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires daily valuation of Scheme assets and liabilities at market prices per fully disclosed and documented methodologies, and daily calculation and declaration of NAV per unit (total assets less liabilities, divided by outstanding units). The Pension Fund may appoint a valuer registered with the IBBI or the Authority, or another specified person.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Daily NAV is a demanding operational cadence and depends on the daily valuation feeding it — the two obligations are linked, and the valuation methodology must be documented and disclosed, not ad hoc.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Value assets and compute/declare NAV daily on a documented, disclosed methodology; appoint an eligible valuer where used.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Daily valuation at market prices; daily NAV per unit; valuer registered with IBBI/Authority

regulation_content.regulation_text:
41. Inspection and investigation

(1) The Authority may, suo motu or upon receipt of information or complaint, undertake
the inspection of the books, accounts, records, documents, infrastructure, procedures and
systems of a Pension Fund, Custodian, Trustee or any other person associated with the

pension ecosystem in the International Financial Services Centres, for any of the
following purpose:

i) ensuring compliance with these regulations;

ii) protecting the interests of the Subscribers; or

iii) any other purpose as deemed fit by the Authority.

(2) The Authority shall also have the power to conduct investigation.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives the Authority power, suo motu or on information/complaint, to inspect the books, records, infrastructure, procedures and systems of a Pension Fund, Custodian, Trustee or other associated person — to ensure compliance, protect subscribers, or for any other purpose it deems fit — and to conduct investigations.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Keep books, records and systems inspection-ready at all times; cooperate with inspection and investigation.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority's inspection and investigation powers

regulation_content.regulation_text:
42. Action in case of default

(1) The Authority may initiate such action as it deems fit, in case a Pension Fund,
Custodian or any other person associated with the pension related activities in
International Financial Services Centre contravenes any of the provisions of these
regulations, subsidiary instruction issued thereunder.

(2) No action referred to under sub-regulation (1) shall be taken without giving a Pension
Fund, Custodian, or any other person associated with the pension related activities in
International Financial Services Centre, as the case may be, a reasonable opportunity of
being heard by way of written submissions.

 CHAPTER IX
 MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets the Authority initiate such action as it deems fit where a Pension Fund, Custodian or other associated person contravenes these Regulations or subsidiary instructions, after giving a reasonable opportunity of being heard by way of written submissions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The trigger is contravention of any provision or subsidiary instruction, so every continuing obligation (net worth, custody, disclosure, risk) feeds into this. The written-submission right is the due-process check.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Treat all continuing obligations as enforceable conditions; use the written-submission opportunity before any adverse order.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Action for contravention, after opportunity of being heard (written submissions)

regulation_content.provision_heading: Power to relax strict enforcement of the regulations
regulation_content.regulation_text:
43. Power to relax strict enforcement of the regulations

(1) The Authority, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may in the interest of
development of pension ecosystem in International Financial Services Centre, relax the
strict enforcement of any provision of these regulations.

(2) For seeking relaxation under sub-regulation (1), an application giving details and the
grounds on which such relaxation is being sought, shall be filed with the Authority along
with such non-refundable fee as may be specified by the Authority.

(3) The application made under sub-regulation (2), complete in all respects, shall be
processed within sixty (60) days from the date of its receipt, or receipt of the responses
to the clarifications sought by the Authority, if any.

(4) The Authority shall dispose of the application received under sub-regulation (2), by
recording the reasons in writing for acceptance or refusal of relaxations sought by the
applicant.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets the Authority, for reasons recorded in writing and in the interest of developing the IFSC pension ecosystem, relax the strict enforcement of any provision. A relaxation application, with grounds, is filed with a non-refundable fee and processed within sixty days of a complete application (or of responses to clarifications); the Authority disposes of it with written reasons.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Relaxation for recorded reasons; application processed within 60 days

regulation_content.regulation_text:
44. Power to call for information

The Authority may call for any information, document or record from a Pension Fund,
Trustee, Custodian or any other person associated with the pension ecosystem in the
International Financial Services Centre.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives the Authority power to call for any information, document or record from a Pension Fund, Trustee, Custodian or other associated person.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority may call for information/records

regulation_content.regulation_text:
45. Power to specify procedures

The Authority may, from time to time, specify norms, procedures, processes or additional
requirements, by way of subsidiary instruction, for the purposes of implementation of
these regulations and matters incidental thereto.

[भाग III—खण्‍ड 4] भारत‍का‍राजपत्र‍:‍असाधारण 47
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets the Authority specify norms, procedures, processes or additional requirements by subsidiary instruction for implementing these Regulations.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Much operative detail will arrive as subsidiary instructions, so compliance monitoring must track these alongside the base text.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority may specify norms/procedures by subsidiary instruction

regulation_content.provision_heading: Power to remove difficulties and issue clarification
regulation_content.regulation_text:
46. Power to remove difficulties and issue clarification

In order to remove any difficulties in the interpretation or application of the provisions
of these regulations, the Authority may issue directions, clarifications, guidance notes or
subsidiary instructions.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets the Authority issue directions, clarifications, guidance notes or subsidiary instructions to remove any difficulty in interpreting or applying these Regulations.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority may issue clarifications/guidance to remove difficulties

regulation_content.regulation_text:
47. Cyber security and cyber resilience

A Pension Fund shall have robust cyber security and cyber resilience framework in
accordance with the requirements as may be specified by the Authority from time to time.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires the Pension Fund to maintain a robust cyber security and cyber resilience framework per the Authority's requirements.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain a cyber security and resilience framework to the Authority's specified standard.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Robust cyber security and cyber resilience framework

regulation_content.regulation_text:
48. Delegation of powers

The powers exercisable by the Authority under these regulations shall also be exercisable
by any officer of the Authority to whom such powers are delegated by the Authority.
